questions.question: If an object of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 10 metres, what will be the ratio of its potential energy and kinetic energy at the height of 5 metres (g = 10m/sec² )
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 : 1**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy (PE)** at a height of 10 meters is given by the formula: PE = m * g * h
 
• For m = 2 kg, g = 10 m/s², and h = 10 m, PE = 2 * 10 * 10 = 200 Joules
 
• **Potential Energy** at a height of 5 meters: PE = m * g * h = 2 * 10 * 5 = 100 Joules
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE)** at a height of 5 meters can be found using the conservation of energy principle: Total Energy at 10 meters = Total Energy at 5 meters
 
• Total Energy = PE at 10 meters = 200 Joules
 
• At 5 meters, Total Energy = PE (5 meters) + KE (5 meters) = 100 + KE
 
• Therefore, KE at 5 meters = 200 - 100 = 100 Joules
 
• The ratio of Potential Energy to Kinetic Energy at 5 meters is PE : KE = 100 : 100 = 1 : 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potential Energy** is the energy possessed by an object due to its position relative to a reference point.
 
• **Kinetic Energy** is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion.
 
• The **law of conservation of energy** states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted from one form to another.
 
• In free fall, the sum of potential energy and kinetic energy remains constant if air resistance is neglected.

questions.question: Which keyboard key is used to jump the cursor to the next cell of the table in MS Word?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tab**__

__
 
• The **Tab** key is used to jump the cursor to the next cell of the table in MS Word.
 
• Using the Tab key allows for quick navigation between cells without using a mouse.
 
• It enhances efficiency when working with tables in documents.
 
• Pressing Tab in the last cell of a table will create a new row.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In addition to moving to the next cell, the Tab key can also be used to indent text within a cell if the cell is not the last one in the row.
 
• To move to the previous cell, the **Shift + Tab** key combination is used.
 
• Other navigation keys like **Arrow keys** can also be used to move between cells, but they do not create new rows.

questions.question: How many languages are included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India as scheduled languages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are currently **22 languages** included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Eighth Schedule lists the official languages recognized by the Indian Constitution.
 
• Initially, the Eighth Schedule included 14 languages, but subsequent amendments have added more languages to the list.
 
• Languages in the Eighth Schedule include Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Tamil, Urdu, Gujarati, Malayalam, Kannada, Odia, Punjabi, Assamese, Maithili, and others.
 
• The recognition of these languages aims to promote and preserve the linguistic diversity of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• Languages added to the Eighth Schedule are often included to recognize the cultural and linguistic significance of various regions and communities in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to acquire citizenship in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Renunciation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Renunciation** is not a way to acquire citizenship in India; rather, it is a way to voluntarily give up Indian citizenship.
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, provides various modes for acquiring Indian citizenship, including **by birth, descent, registration, and naturalization**.
 
• **Incorporation of territory** is another mode where a new territory becomes a part of India, and the government may specify the persons who shall be citizens of India.
 
• Citizenship by **registration** is available to certain categories of persons such as persons of Indian origin who are ordinarily resident in India and other specified categories.
 
• Citizenship by **birth** is applicable to individuals born in India on or after January 26, 1950, but before July 1, 1987, and to individuals born on or after July 1, 1987, if either parent is a citizen of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, also provides for the termination and deprivation of citizenship under specific conditions.
 
• Renunciation of citizenship is a voluntary act and can be done by any citizen of India who is also a citizen or national of another country.
 
• Upon renunciation, the individual ceases to be a citizen of India, and any minor child of that person also loses Indian citizenship.
 
• The process of renunciation is outlined in the Citizenship Rules, and it requires the individual to make a declaration in the prescribed manner.
 
• It's important for individuals to be aware of the implications of renunciation, including the loss of rights and privileges associated with Indian citizenship.

questions.question: The point in the orbit of an object (such as a satellite) orbiting the earth that is at the greatest distance from the centre of the earth is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**apogee**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The point in the orbit of an object (such as a satellite) orbiting the earth that is at the greatest distance from the centre of the earth is known as **apogee**.
 
• Apogee is derived from the Greek words "apo," meaning away, and "ge," meaning Earth.
 
• It contrasts with **perigee**, which is the point in the orbit of an object where it is closest to the Earth.
 
• Understanding apogee and perigee is crucial for satellite operations and space missions, as it affects communication signals and orbital dynamics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aphelion** and **perihelion** are terms used to describe the farthest and nearest points of an object's orbit around the Sun, respectively.
 
• The term **perigee** is used specifically for objects orbiting the Earth, while **perihelion** is for objects orbiting the Sun.
 
• Knowledge of these orbital points is important for understanding the mechanics of celestial bodies and for planning space missions.
 
• Orbital mechanics is a fundamental aspect of astrophysics and aerospace engineering, guiding the design and operation of spacecraft. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5219344328d7b028b2e0108b7d3f644db77d319429544bd6dd9d139def38ff4.png]

questions.question:
With reference to the Directive Principles of State policy contained in the Constitution of India, which of the following statements is/are correct?

1. Article 37 of the Constitution of India provides that the Directive Principles of State Policy are enforceable in the High Courts only.

2. Article 38 provides that the State shall strive to minimise the inequalities in income amongst individuals and groups of people.

3. Article 39 provides that the State shall direct its policy towards securing that there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2 and 3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 37** of the Constitution of India explicitly states that the Directive Principles of State Policy are not enforceable by any court, but the principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.
 
• **Article 38** provides that the State shall strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order in which justice, social, economic, and political, shall inform all the institutions of national life. It also directs the State to minimize inequalities in income, and endeavor to eliminate inequalities in status, facilities, and opportunities, not only amongst individuals but also amongst groups of people residing in different areas or engaged in different vocations.
 
• **Article 39** mandates the State to direct its policy towards securing that men and women equally have the right to an adequate means of livelihood, that there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women, and that the health and strength of workers, men and women, and the tender age of children are not abused.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government and are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, though they are non-justiciable in nature.
 
• These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life. They also aim to establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state.
 
• The principles have been inspired by the Directive Principles given in the Constitution of Ireland and also by the principles of Gandhism.
 
• While the Directive Principles are non-justiciable, they act as a guide to the state in the matter of governance and law-making and are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The Constitution aims to achieve the goal of a welfare state by implementing these principles.

questions.question: Easter is a religious festival of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Christians**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Easter** is a religious festival celebrated by **Christians**.
 
• It commemorates the resurrection of **Jesus Christ** from the dead, described in the New Testament as having occurred on the third day after his burial following his crucifixion by the Romans at Calvary c. 30 AD.
 
• Easter is the culmination of the **Passion of Jesus**, preceded by Lent (or Great Lent), a 40-day period of fasting, prayer, and penance.
 
• The week before Easter is known as **Holy Week**, and it contains the days of the Easter Triduum, including **Maundy Thursday** (commemorating the Maundy and Last Supper), and Good Friday (commemorating the crucifixion and death of Jesus).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Easter is linked to the Jewish Passover by much of its symbolism, as well as by its position in the calendar.
 
• In many languages, the words for "Easter" and "Passover" are identical or very similar.
 
• Easter customs vary across the Christian world, and include sunrise services, exclaiming the Paschal greeting, clipping the church, and decorating Easter eggs.
 
• The Easter lily, a symbol of the resurrection in Western Christianity, traditionally decorates the chancel area of churches on Easter Day and throughout the Eastertide season.
 
• Additional customs include egg hunting, the Easter Bunny, and Easter parades.

questions.question: Rotating Savings and Credit Association (ROSCA) was introduced by Shirley Ardener in the year ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1964**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rotating Savings and Credit Association (ROSCA)** was introduced by Shirley Ardener in the year **1964**.
 
• ROSCA is a group of individuals who come together to save and borrow collectively from a common fund.
 
• Each member of the group contributes a fixed amount to the fund at regular intervals, and one member gets the entire sum collected at each interval.
 
• This process continues until all members have received the sum once.
 
• ROSCA is a traditional form of savings and credit, widely practiced in various parts of the world, particularly in developing countries.
 
• It provides an alternative to formal banking systems, particularly for individuals who may not have access to traditional financial services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shirley Ardener** is an anthropologist and researcher who has extensively studied and documented ROSCAs.
 
• ROSCAs are known by various names in different cultures, such as "tandas" in Latin America, "susus" in West Africa, and "chit funds" in India.
 
• They play a crucial role in financial inclusion by providing a mechanism for saving and accessing credit outside of formal financial institutions.
 
• ROSCAs can also foster a sense of community and mutual support among members.
 
• Despite their benefits, ROSCAs also carry risks, such as the potential for members to default on their contributions.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah**__

__
 
• **Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah** was the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate.
 
• The Bahmani Sultanate was established in **1347** in the Deccan region of South India.
 
• Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah originally served as a commander under the Delhi Sultanate before declaring independence.
 
• The Bahmani Sultanate was one of the major medieval Indian kingdoms and was known for its cultural contributions and architectural advancements.
 
• The Sultanate played a significant role in the history of the Deccan region and laid the foundation for the Deccan Sultanates that followed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Bahmani Sultanate was divided into five smaller kingdoms known as the **Deccan Sultanates** after its decline.
 
• The capital of the Bahmani Sultanate was initially **Gulbarga** and later shifted to **Bidar**.
 
• The Bahmani rulers were known for their patronage of Persian culture and language, which greatly influenced the region's art, architecture, and literature.
 
• The Bahmani Sultanate engaged in frequent conflicts with the Vijayanagara Empire, another major kingdom in South India.
 
• The legacy of the Bahmani Sultanate can still be seen in the form of various monuments, forts, and mosques scattered across the Deccan region.

questions.question: In which year was the 15th National Census Survey of India conducted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2011**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **2011** was the year when the 15th National Census Survey of India was conducted.
 
• The National Census Survey is conducted every ten years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The census collects comprehensive demographic data which is crucial for planning and policy-making.
 
• The data includes information on population, economic activity, literacy and education, housing and household amenities, urbanization, fertility and mortality, and many other socio-economic parameters.
 
• The first census in India was conducted in 1872, and since 1881, it has been conducted every ten years without a break.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **2021 census** was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic, making the 2011 census the most recent one.
 
• India's census is one of the largest administrative exercises in the world.
 
• The census data is used for redrawing constituencies, allocation of government resources, and various other administrative functions.
 
• The census also provides a detailed picture of the socio-economic and demographic changes over the decade.
 
• Data from the census is used extensively for academic research and by international organizations.

questions.question: Select the musical instrument which is NOT played by way of percussion or NOT played by way of striking any object?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shehnai**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shehnai** is a wind instrument, which means it is played by blowing air into it, not by percussion or striking.
 
• The other options listed, such as **Pakhawaj, Drum, and Tabla**, are all percussion instruments that produce sound by being struck.
 
• The **Shehnai** is commonly used in traditional Indian music, especially in auspicious occasions and ceremonies.
 
• It has a distinct, melodious sound that is different from the rhythmic beats produced by percussion instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Shehnai** is believed to bring good luck and is an integral part of North Indian weddings and festivals.
 
• It is made of wood with a double reed at one end and a metal or wooden flared bell at the other end.
 
• The instrument has been popularized globally by renowned musicians like **Ustad Bismillah Khan**.
 
• Learning to play the Shehnai requires significant practice and skill, as the musician must control the breath and finger movements precisely.

questions.question: Which of the following is a cyclic arrangement of time units in Hindustani classical music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tala** is the term used in Hindustani classical music to denote a cyclic arrangement of time units.
 
• It serves as a rhythmic framework for the performance and is essential for the structuring of the music.
 
• Each tala is characterized by a specific number of beats, known as **matras**, which are grouped into sections called **vibhags**.
 
• Common talas in Hindustani music include **Teentaal, Ektaal, and Jhaptaal**.
 
• The tala system is crucial for both the composition and improvisation in performances, guiding the timing and rhythm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hindustani classical music, one of the two main sub-genres of Indian classical music, has a rich tradition and history dating back to the Vedic times.
 
• It is characterized by a wide variety of **ragas (melodic frameworks)** and **talas (rhythmic cycles)**, each with specific rules and structures.
 
• Unlike Western classical music, Hindustani music places a significant emphasis on improvisation within the set frameworks of raga and tala.
 
• The performance of a piece in Hindustani classical music often involves a gradual development from slow, meditative sections to fast, intricate passages.
 
• This genre of music has been influenced by various cultural and historical factors, including Persian and Mughal traditions.

questions.question: What is the penalty for a wide ball in cricket?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One run**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **One run** is awarded to the batting team for a wide ball in cricket.
 
• A wide ball is a delivery that the umpire judges to be too wide or high to be hit by the batsman by means of a normal cricket shot.
 
• In addition to the one run, an extra delivery is also bowled to compensate for the wide ball.
 
• The rule ensures fairness and maintains the challenge for the bowler to deliver within the acceptable area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Laws of Cricket** are maintained by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) and are known as the **Code of Laws**.
 
• Wide ball rules are specified in **Law 22** of the MCC's Laws of Cricket.
 
• Wide balls contribute to the batting team's total score and can impact the game's outcome significantly.
 
• Other penalties in cricket include no-balls, which also result in extra runs and an extra delivery.
 
• The umpire signals a wide ball by extending both arms horizontally.
